# BAD-094 — main pushes a room's collab:changed diff before the status reply the renderer is awaiting

## Brief
main.js's collab:status handler calls collabPushChanged(events) and THEN returns the status. A webContents.send is delivered to the renderer before the invoke reply resolves, so the renderer reacts to a room's news while the very call that produced it is still outstanding. onCollabChanged then fires refreshCollab, which bumps collab.seq and can supersede the refresh that is still in flight. BAD-090 had to route around this (the sync pulls outside refreshCollab rather than inside it) and named it in renderer/CLAUDE.md, but the ordering itself is untouched and will bite the next thing that assumes an invoke reply lands before its side effects. Worth either deferring the push to a microtask after the reply is returned, or having onCollabChanged skip a room whose status call is still outstanding. Neither is BAD-090's business and neither should be done without deciding which of the two is the real rule.

Evidence: main.js:3556-3558 (the absorbCollabInfo + collabPushChanged pair inside ipcMain.handle('collab:status')). src/collab.js diffCollabInfo emits part_progress exactly when another member's take count rises, so the read that FIRST sees a collaborator's take is the one that fires the event. renderer/app.js:6389 onCollabChanged -> refreshCollab(pack, {pull:false}) -> ++collab.seq. BADS-090/Desiree confirmed the delivery order with a minimal Electron experiment: ORDER:[changed-listener, status-reply]. Related and smaller: absorbCollabInfo (main.js:4453) has no monotonicity guard, so a pollCollabInfosOnce info fetch already in flight when collab:status absorbs will overwrite the newer snapshot when it resolves — now that collab:pull decides from that store, worst case is one take one cycle late.
